question: Who among the following was the first Chinese Citizen to win Nobel Peace Prize?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liu Xiaobo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Liu Xiaobo** was a Chinese literary critic, writer, human rights activist, and Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize in 2010** for his long and non-violent struggle for fundamental human rights in China.
 
• At the time of the award, Liu Xiaobo was imprisoned in China, having been sentenced in 2009 to 11 years for "inciting subversion of state power".
 
• His wife, **Liu Xia**, was placed under house arrest shortly after the award was announced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nobel Peace Prize**

 
 
• The Nobel Peace Prize is one of the five Nobel Prizes established by the will of Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite, in 1895.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Norwegian Nobel Committee to individuals or organizations that have made significant contributions to peace efforts.
 
• The prize includes a medal, a diploma, and a monetary award.
 
• Past laureates include prominent figures such as Martin Luther King Jr., Mother Teresa, and Malala Yousafzai.
 
 
 
• **Human Rights Activism in China**
 
 
• Human rights activism in China is a sensitive and often dangerous endeavor due to the Chinese government's strict control over political dissent and social activism.
 
• Activists like Liu Xiaobo have faced imprisonment, surveillance, and other forms of repression.
 
• Despite these challenges, many continue to advocate for democratic reforms, freedom of speech, and other basic human rights in China.
 
• International organizations often highlight these efforts and call for the release of imprisoned activists.
 
 
 
• **Liu Xiaobo's Legacy**
 
 
• Liu Xiaobo's legacy is marked by his commitment to non-violent protest and his advocacy for democratic reforms in China.
 
• His writings and activism have inspired many within China and around the world to continue the fight for human rights.
 
• His Nobel Peace Prize drew international attention to the plight of political prisoners in China.
 
• Liu Xiaobo passed away in 2017 while still in custody, but his work continues to influence human rights movements globally.
